title: Rotate the payment gateway API key
purpose: Replace the live payment gateway key without dropping checkout traffic, e.g. after a suspected leak or on the 90-day schedule.
trigger: The security channel reports a possible key exposure, or the calendar reminder for the quarterly rotation fires.
preconditions: You have the `payments-admin` role in the gateway console
The `ops` VPN is connected (the config service is not reachable otherwise)
Checkout error rate is at baseline (below 0.5% on the dashboard) — do not rotate during an incident

steps.do: Create a new key in the gateway console at `Settings → API keys → Create` and copy it once; it is shown only once.
steps.verify: The console lists two active keys: the old one and the new one, both marked live.
steps.ifFails: If the console refuses (key limit reached), delete the oldest *inactive* key first — never an active one — and retry.

steps.do: Write the new key to the config service: `opsctl secret set payments/gateway_key --from-stdin`, pasting the key.
steps.verify: `opsctl secret get payments/gateway_key --meta` shows a new version number and a timestamp within the last minute.
steps.ifFails: If `opsctl` reports a permissions error, your VPN session has expired; reconnect and retry. Do not paste the key into chat to hand off.

steps.do: Roll the checkout service so it picks up the new secret: `opsctl rollout restart checkout --wait`.
steps.verify: `opsctl rollout status checkout` reports all replicas ready, and the dashboard's checkout error rate stays below 0.5% for five minutes.
steps.ifFails: If error rate rises, run the Rollback section immediately; do not wait out the five minutes.

steps.do: Revoke the old key in the gateway console at `Settings → API keys → <old key> → Revoke`.
steps.verify: The console lists exactly one active key, and the error rate is still at baseline after five more minutes.
steps.ifFails: If revoking the old key raises the error rate, some caller still uses it: re-enable it (Revoke is reversible for 24 hours) and search the config service for other consumers of `payments/gateway_key`.

rollback: Set the previous secret version back with `opsctl secret rollback payments/gateway_key --to <previous-version>` and restart checkout (`opsctl rollout restart checkout --wait`). If the old key was already revoked, re-enable it in the console first (possible within 24 hours of revocation).

escalation.when: Error rate above 2% for more than two minutes at any step, or the old key cannot be re-enabled.
